summary: Sangarius (Ancient Greek Σαγγάριος) is the Phrygian river-god who personifies the Sangarius (modern Sakarya) in northwestern Asia Minor. Hesiod numbers him among the sons of Oceanus and Tethys; mythographers make him father or grandfather of Hecuba and, in other strands, ancestor of Attis through Nana and father of Nicaea by Cybele.
etymology: The river's name is said in one etymology to come from Sangas, a man Rhea punished by turning into water. The god Sangarius is the divine personification of that Phrygian stream.

sections.heading: Genealogy
paragraphs: In the Theogony Sangarius is an Oceanid river-son of Oceanus and Tethys. Apollodorus makes him husband of Metope and father of Hecuba; other notes name the naiad Evagora as mother, or give him a daughter Eunoë who bears Hecabe to King Dymas.
Ovid's Fasti connects him with Nana and thus with Attis. Nonnus has him father Nicaea by Cybele; other children in the tradition include Sagaritis and Ocyrrhoe.

sections.heading: Mythic geography
paragraphs: Homer's Iliad camps Trojan allies beside the Sangarius, tying the river to the Anatolian hinterland of Priam's world. The god and the stream are the same mythic fact: a major Phrygian watercourse on the road between the Aegean and the Anatolian plateau.
The atlas id sangarius is this river-god. He is not a mortal king or a separate city eponym.
